route: Work permit and residence permit (Ministry of Labour)

permit.applies: The employer applies online to the Ministry of Labour and Industrial Relations through the National E-Licensing System (NELS); the residence permit application to the Passport and Immigration Office goes with it automatically.
permit.first: Proof the employer tried to recruit locally through the National Employment Department, the vacancy advertised on mauritiusjobs.govmu.org; a vetted contract where the salary is MUR 50,000 a month or less.

fees.what: Annual fee on approval (non-refundable), with the prescribed work permit fee

permit.validityNote: Renewed online, the application filed three months before expiry; ten years' stay at most in all sectors; a permit lapses if not taken up within six months.
permit.eligibility: Generally aged between 20 and 60; no work permit for a holder of a tourist or student visa.
permit.feesNote: The prescribed work permit fee itself, in the Non-Citizens (Work Permit) (Fees) Regulations 2013, wasn't read.

sources.title: Ministry of Labour and Industrial Relations (Employment Division), Work Permit Information Sheet: Summary of Main Procedures and Checklist of Documents (February 2026), linked from https://empment-labour.govmu.org/Pages/Work%20Permit/ApplicationWP.aspx
sources.said: The non-citizen should generally be aged between 20 and 60 years … Accordingly, applications for a work permit in respect of holders of a tourist visa or student visa will not be entertained. It is to be noted that if the holder of a Work Permit does not travel to Mauritius to take up employment within 6 months of the date of issue of the Work Permit, same will lapse. After completion of the maximum ten years of stay and work in Mauritius, the worker should leave the country … Applications for New, Renewal and Transfer Cases of Work Permit have to be submitted online via the National E-Licensing platform (NELS) upon registration at https://business.edbmauritius.org. … The requirement to obtain a Permission in Principle prior to submitting a Work Permit application is no longer applicable. In addition, the existing quota/ratio system has been abolished, and the maximum allowable period of stay for foreign workers across all sectors has been standardised at ten (10) years. Employers must, however, demonstrate their inability to recruit locally. … a processing fee of Rs 700 should be paid per application within 5 days of post verification of completeness of applications. Upon approval of application, a non-refundable annual fee of Rs. 500 should be paid together with the prescribed work permit fees. … Applications for renewal of work permits should be submitted 3 months prior to the expiry of the current one.

sources.title: Ministry of Labour and Industrial Relations, Application of Work Permit (page)
sources.said: All applications for new or renewal of work permits/certificates of exemption must be submitted online through the National E-Licensing System (NELS ), accessible on https://business.edbmauritius.org.

note: The Economic Development Board's occupation permits (including a short-term one) are another route for professionals; not modelled for performers, no primary read. An error found and fixed on 2026-11-04: the route was held as the UFE's country file had it, with the Ministry's agreement in principle first and a permit of at most four years (five in the free zone); the Ministry's own Information Sheet (February 2026) says there is no Permission in Principle or quota any more, the employer applying online after trying to recruit locally, with ten years' stay at most, so the UFE's file was dropped. The prescribed permit fee, the decision time, any union step, pay rule or short engagement free of it weren't found.
